title: Pushout of a monomorphism in an abelian category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] (for instance $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ for a scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], which has all small colimits), let $a:G\to G'$ be a monomorphism and $b:G\to F$ any morphism of $\mathcal A$, and let $F'=G'\amalg_GF$ be the pushout of $a$ and $b$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with canonical maps $a':F\to F'$ and $b':G'\to F'$, $a'\circ b=b'\circ a$. Then $a':F\to F'$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), proof, first paragraph ('Then we can take F' to be the pushout F' = G' amalg_G F'); the fact used (left implicit by Stacks) is that the pushout of a monomorphism in an abelian category is a monomorphism; with the description of pushouts in Homology, Example 05PJ (label example-fibre-product-pushouts, literature/stacks-project/homology.tex line 700) as Coker((a,-b):G -> G' + F)
